items.summary: On Nov 20, Indonesia's Forest Area Enforcement Task Force (Satgas PKH) revoked the forestry permit covering [q1: 338,536ha] held by Riau Andalan Pulp and Paper (RAPP), a subsidiary of Asia Pacific Resources International Limited (APRIL) Group. The area is about [q2: 4.5 times] the size of Singapore, with the entire concession in Riau province returning to state control under a Forestry Ministerial Decree dated Nov 19. Grounds cited include recurring peatland fires, oil palm plantations spanning [q3: 18,362.74ha], unauthorised mining activities covering [q4: 541.46ha], and damage to protected areas spanning [q5: 211.54ha]. The task force noted the revocation does not absolve RAPP of environmental restoration obligations or potential legal liabilities, amid heightened scrutiny over forest fires and transboundary haze. APRIL Group said it learned of the decision through media reports and was awaiting formal notification.
items.title: Indonesia revokes Riau forestry permits of APRIL Group unit over alleged peatland fires and violations

items.summary: Sources familiar with the matter report that Singapore-based DayOne Data Centers has put its planned US initial public offering on hold, as investors question whether frothy valuations for digital infrastructure supporting the artificial intelligence boom are sustainable. The company had initially intended to raise as much as $5 billion (S$6.5 billion) from an IPO as soon as the fourth quarter of 2024, but began reassessing options including a delay or smaller listing amid rising volatility around data centre and AI stocks. DayOne may still pursue an IPO in 2027 if market sentiment improves; deliberations are ongoing with no final decisions made, though a company representative declined to comment. The Nasdaq 100 has dropped more than 6% in November, heading for its worst November performance since 2008, while Anthropic staged a record-breaking $107.3 billion IPO and private placement and rose 17% on its Nov 19 trading debut to become the world's seventh-most valuable company.
items.title: DayOne pauses multibillion-dollar US IPO amid data centre and AI market volatility.

items.summary: On [d1: 20th November 2026], mathematician Levent Alpöge posted that he believes he has discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis while working with Claude. He claims the method extends to resolve the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis and, with more time, possibly the Extended Riemann Hypothesis. The arguments were formalized without assumptions; Alpöge says Claude outpaced him near the finish line. These are stated as his own beliefs and expectations rather than established results.
items.title: Alpöge claims a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis with Claude, dated 20th November 2026

items.summary: Bloomberg reported that Spotify co-founder Daniel Ek is backing Europa Fusion, a stealthy U.K.-based fusion power startup founded in February by Nantas Nardelli. Nardelli brings extensive AI experience from Google DeepMind, Facebook AI Research, and Microsoft Research Cambridge, and most recently served as head of machine learning at Pacific Fusion, which broke ground on a demonstration facility in New Mexico. He reportedly diverged from Pacific Fusion's hardware-heavy testing approach, favoring instead a simulation- and data-intensive method; Europa Fusion will pursue pulsed-power fusion using timed electrical surges to compress fuel targets until they fuse and release energy. The venture is attributed by Nardelli to the goal of carbon-free power with near-limitless fuel supplies that could also ease AI's growing energy demands, though no one has yet built a grid-supplying fusion plant; he described his pivot from building robots as being "time to fix climate change for good."
items.title: Spotify founder Daniel Ek backs AI researcher's fusion power startup

items.summary: Mathematician Levent Alpöge announced what he describes as a Lean-compilable proof of the 167-year-old Riemann hypothesis (originally posed in 1859), one of the Millennium Prize problems. He wrote that announcing his findings came at "horrible" timing because he had messaged Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei last Sunday night to ask how to reveal a solution compiled in Lean, an open-source language used to formally verify mathematical proofs. The proof relies on a cohomology bound proved by what appears to be an automorphy-lifting argument drawing on Galois representations and several other established results; the essay notes that without being expressed in Lean it is too early to say whether the proof checks out or if anyone understands it, though most participants appear confident the formalized result will hold. Alpöge described a "stream-of-consciousness jaunt through the experience of finding all the pieces of the argument" with Claude, while committing to pursue a human-intelligible explanation before release; he also released another proof related to Navier-Stokes equations alongside collaborator Tristan Buckmaster. In contrast, Ravi Vakil posted Alessandro Masullo's General Riemann hypothesis draft as "all human, with no AI," the result of 12 years of work meant partly for mathematicians discouraged by the current climate; Vakil noted that now seems best to release the current draft rather than wait to polish it at Stanford. The story was updated to note that Alpöge's Lean proof has been checked by independent sources, including MIT mathematician Andrew Sutherland and others who confirmed it compiles successfully.
items.title: Levent Alpöge claims a formalized solution to Riemann's hypothesis, with AI assistance

items.summary: For Black Friday, Kia, Lucid, and Volkswagen are offering discounts of $10,000 or more on select electric vehicles. Lucid is providing a $15,000 credit toward the 2027 Gravity Touring (starting at $79,900) and a $10,000 credit for the 2027 Air Touring ($79,900), both ending November 30. Kia is applying $10,000 discounts to its EV9 lineup—dropping the base Light RWD trim to as low as $44,900 from a $54,900 MSRP—and to the Niro EV (as low as $29,700 from $39,700), with deals running until January 4. Volkswagen is offering a $10,000 bonus on its final-year 2026 ID.4, though inventory is limited and offers end November 30. The article notes that EV sales rebounded to nearly 263,000 units in the third quarter—most since Q3 2025—and that October's average transaction price fell 2.9% year-over-year to $56,221.
items.title: Kia, Lucid, and Volkswagen are slashing EV prices by $10,000+ for Black Friday
